newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel evicts bedouin to expand Jewish settlement.
newsitem.headline: Israel evicts bedouin to expand Jewish settlement.

text.p: Israel evicted a Palestinian bedouin family and destroyed its West Bank encampment on Tuesday to make room for expansion of a Jewish settlement in the Israeli-occupied territory, witnesses said.
The move took place as Israel and the PLO neared a deal on future Israeli troop redeployments in West Bank rural areas.
Witnesses said Israeli police forced a Palestinian woman and her two babies to move into a nearby site Israel designated for the bedouin of the Jahalin tribe.

An Israeli bulldozer flattened three shacks after policemen hauled the family's livestock and belongings away on a truck. Police also detained three members of the tribe who tried to resist the eviction, witnesses said.
"They are uprooting us from our homes by force," said Ali Abu Ghaliyeh, a 39-year-old school teacher who was being held on a police bus.
A spokesman for Israel's civil administration in the West Bank said the eviction came after the Jahalin tribe lost a legal battle in Israel's Supreme Court last September.
Spokesman Peter Lerner told reporters the tribe was squatting on state land designated since 1981 for the expansion of nearby Maaleh Adumim settlement.

He said Israel wanted to move about 20 other families to the new location. Palestinians say up to 350 bedouin live in the wilderness between the Arab villages of Aizariyeh and Abu Dis east of Jerusalem.

Human rights lawyer Linda Breyer charged Israel was trying to move Palestinians out of West Bank areas under its control in advance of Israeli-PLO peace talks on the fate of rural areas in the occupied territory.
"I call this ethnic cleansing," she said.
Lerner said there was no connection between the bedouin eviction and negotiations on the West Bank's future.
"One has nothing to do with the other," he said.
